name: HEhub
listed_description: A library for homomorphic encryption and its applications.
reason: No comparison against any named baseline. The README benchmark section (raw README plus the github.com repo page) gives only absolute timings for HEhub on an Intel i7-9750H with Clang 12.0.5 (NTT 7 us at N=1024 up to 330 us at N=32768; CKKS encode+encrypt 426 us at N=4096) and states 'The code for benchmark is still incomplete'. The bench/ sources (ntt_bm.cpp, ckks_bm.cpp, mod_arith_bm.cpp, benchmarks.cpp) are small; the first three are fully commented-out Catch2 code and benchmarks.cpp uses nanobench, and none references SEAL, OpenFHE, HElib or Lattigo. The four newest develop commits (2026-05-12) are titled '[opt] ...' (CKKS FFT, OpenMP, march=native/LTO) but their titles carry no numbers. A WebSearch for HEhub or primihub against SEAL and OpenFHE returned only third-party SEAL vs OpenFHE papers that do not include HEhub.

name: Libgcrypt
listed_description: A general purpose cryptographic library originally based on code from GnuPG.
reason: No reachable numeric comparison against an external baseline. NEWS (raw.githubusercontent.com/gpg/libgcrypt/HEAD/NEWS) lists only speedups over its own earlier releases (AES-XTS 6 times faster with AES-NI, SHA-1/SHA-256 4.0/3.7 times faster with Intel SHA extensions, SHA-512 4.5 times faster on Ryzen 7, VAES/AVX512 about 2 times OCB on AMD Zen5). The jkivilin/bench-slopes README (libgcrypt, OpenSSL, Nettle, Botan, Crypto++ drivers) only prints example outputs from different machines and library versions, not a head-to-head, and the scc-tw/cryptobench-cpp suite (result.json) has no libgcrypt column. Candidate comparisons all sit on hosts that do not resolve here (ENOTFOUND for gnupg.org, lists.gnupg.org, lists.lysator.liu.se, panthema.net); only WebSearch summaries were seen and nothing was verified: the 2013 'Speedups in Libgcrypt 1.6' blog on gnupg.org (says libgcrypt had long trailed OpenSSL and Nettle was faster in places), a 2017 nettle-bugs thread (AES-128-CBC with AES-NI on an i7-6820HQ: nettle 850, libgcrypt 1172, gnutls 1230, openssl 1153 MB/s, so libgcrypt about 1.7 percent above OpenSSL), and the 2008 panthema.net crypto speedtest (libgcrypt reported much slower than Botan, Crypto++, LibTomCrypt). Retry from an environment that can open them. Suggested category aead-and-ciphers; LGPL-2.1-or-later.

name: LibreSSL
listed_description: A free version of the SSL/TLS protocol forked from OpenSSL in 2014.
reason: No numeric claim of being faster than OpenSSL. The README and ChangeLog (raw.githubusercontent.com/libressl/portable/HEAD) mention performance only qualitatively ('Significantly improved Montgomery multiplication performance', 'Improve SHA-3 performance by using an unrolled and interleaved algorithm', new SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-512 amd64 assembly using SHA-NI) with no figures or baseline. KazKobara/plot-openssl-speed (github.com README) says LibreSSL 2.9.1 and newer shows aes-128/256-gcm 'by far faster' and 'similar results as OpenSSL 1', but states no numbers and its figures are PNGs stored as git-lfs pointers (unreachable), and the sentence does not say which library or cipher it is compared with. Where numbers surfaced they favour OpenSSL: WebSearch snippets only, not opened, of a FreeBSD forum post (AES-128-CBC 8 KB about 413 MB/s OpenSSL 1.0.2k vs about 22 MB/s LibreSSL 2.6.4 without AES-NI) and a Phoronix forum comment (OpenSSL 1.1.1 ECDSA up to 380 percent faster than LibreSSL 2.7). The HAProxy 'State of SSL Stacks' paper (OpenSSL 3.x vs LibreSSL, WolfSSL, AWS-LC) and the Phoronix LibreSSL 4.1 article could not be opened (ENOTFOUND for cdn.haproxy.com, www.haproxy.com, www.phoronix.com); retry them for handshake and SHA-NI numbers.

name: LibTomCrypt
listed_description: A fairly comprehensive, modular and portable cryptographic toolkit.
reason: Directional claim only. doc/crypt.tex (raw.githubusercontent.com/libtom/libtomcrypt/HEAD/doc/crypt.tex) says the library 'has been clocked on various platforms with cycles per byte timings that are comparable (and often favourable) to other libraries such as OpenSSL and Crypto++', with no numbers, versions or hardware, and the same document says the author is 'not striving to replace OpenSSL or Crypto++'. The README only describes a `timing` binary that measures MPI providers against GMP, with no stored results. No shootout including LibTomCrypt was reachable: scc-tw/cryptobench-cpp, jkivilin/bench-slopes and briansmith/crypto-bench do not cover it; the 2008 panthema.net speedtest (WebSearch summary only, host does not resolve here) reportedly has LibTomCrypt, Botan and Crypto++ performing well ahead of libgcrypt and Nettle, but no numbers were seen.

name: Nettle
reason: No reachable numeric comparison against an external baseline. NEWS and ChangeLog (gitlab.com/gnutls/nettle/-/raw/master) give only speedups over earlier releases or over its own C code (3.7 release: 13 times for AES256-CTR and AES256-GCM and 3.5 times for ChaCha on a Power9 machine; sha_ni 3-5 times; x86_64 ecc assembly 2.4 to 5 times over C). examples/nettle-benchmark and hogweed-benchmark can time OpenSSL through glue code, but no results are stored; briansmith/crypto-bench has an empty rust-nettle column. WebSearch summaries (nettle-bugs list on lists.lysator.liu.se, host does not resolve here, nothing opened) show Nettle behind OpenSSL (AES-128-CBC with AES-NI 850 vs 1153 MB/s on an i7-6820HQ, 2017; ChaCha 6.59 vs 1.20 cycles/byte on an i7-4790K, 2019) and one POWER9 Poly1305 patch (2022) at 0.972 vs OpenSSL 1.453 cycles/byte, unverified and from a review thread rather than a release claim. Retry the lysator mailing-list thread from an environment that can open it.
